title: Reaction Types & Chemical Equations

competencies.text: Use chemical equations for photosynthesis and respiration.
Describe metabolic reactions in body cells and their significance.

days.title: Reading and Balancing Equations
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will use chemical equations for photosynthesis and respiration and describe metabolic reactions in body cells.

🧪 Parts of a Chemical Equation

2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O

  • Formulas (H₂, O₂, H₂O) show which atoms are in each substance. The small subscript tells how many atoms are in one molecule.
  • Coefficients (the big 2s) tell how many molecules react.
  • The arrow means "react to form." Reactants are on the left, products on the right.

⚖️ Law of Conservation of Mass

Atoms are neither created nor destroyed, so each kind of atom must appear the same number of times on both sides. In 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O: left has 4 H and 2 O; right has 4 H and 2 O. Balanced!

🛠️ How to Balance

  1. Count each atom on both sides.
  2. Change coefficients only — never subscripts (changing H₂O to H₂O₂ makes a different substance).
  3. Recount until every atom matches.

Example: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O (methane burning). Left: 1 C, 4 H, 4 O. Right: 1 C, 4 H, 4 O.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: Why must a chemical equation be balanced?

choices.label: Atoms are not created or destroyed
Products must weigh more than reactants
Every equation needs an even number
Coefficients make the reaction go faster

scenario.explanation: Balancing shows the law of conservation of mass: the same atoms appear before and after, only rearranged.

scenario.text: In 3O₂, what does the 3 tell you?

choices.label: There are three oxygen molecules
Each molecule has three oxygen atoms
The reaction happens three times faster
Oxygen has a charge of three in this case

scenario.explanation: The coefficient counts molecules. 3O₂ means three O₂ molecules — six oxygen atoms in all.

choices.label: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
H₂ + O₂ → H₂O
H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
2H₂ + 2O₂ → H₂O

scenario.explanation: Left: 4 H and 2 O. Right: 4 H and 2 O. Every atom is accounted for.

days.title: Photosynthesis and Cellular Respiration
days.content:
🌿 Photosynthesis (in chloroplasts)

6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

Plants, algae and some bacteria use light energy captured by chlorophyll to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose (stored chemical energy) and release oxygen.

🔥 Cellular Respiration (mostly in mitochondria)

C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy (ATP)

Nearly all living cells — plant and animal — break down glucose with oxygen to release energy stored as ATP, the cell's energy currency.

🔄 Opposite but Connected

PhotosynthesisRespiration
EnergyStored (light → chemical)Released (chemical → ATP)
Takes inCO₂ and H₂OGlucose and O₂
Gives offGlucose and O₂CO₂ and H₂O
Who does itProducers onlyAlmost all organisms, including plants

The products of one are the reactants of the other — this cycle links plants and animals through the air.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its meaning. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Substance on the left side of the arrow
match.why: Reactants are used up in the reaction.

match.right: Substance on the right side of the arrow
match.why: Products are formed by the reaction.

match.right: Number in front of a formula to balance it
match.why: It counts molecules, not atoms in one molecule.
Light energy is stored in glucose.
Energy in glucose is released as ATP.

match.right: Organelle where most ATP is made

match.why: Cells spend ATP to move, build and transport.

days.title: Metabolism in Body Cells
days.content:
⚙️ What Is Metabolism?

Metabolism is all the chemical reactions in a living body. It has two sides:

  • Catabolism — breaking big molecules into small ones, releasing energy (digesting starch into glucose; respiration).
  • Anabolism — building big molecules from small ones, using energy (making proteins from amino acids; building muscle).

🧬 Enzymes

Body reactions would be far too slow at 37 °C without enzymes — protein catalysts. Amylase in saliva starts breaking down rice starch in your mouth. Enzymes work best at body temperature and the right pH; a high fever can change their shape and slow them down.

🏃 When Oxygen Runs Short

During a hard sprint, muscles need ATP faster than oxygen arrives. Cells switch to anaerobic respiration: glucose → lactic acid + a little ATP. It is fast but makes much less energy, and lactic acid causes the burning feeling. Heavy breathing afterward brings in oxygen to recover. Yeast does a similar process — fermentation — making alcohol and CO₂, used in bread and tuba.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Apply the equations and metabolism ideas. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A plant in a sealed glass box is left in sunlight all day. What happens to the CO₂ level inside?

choices.label: It goes down as the plant uses it for photosynthesis
It goes up as the plant breathes out much more CO₂
It stays exactly the same because plants do not breathe
It drops to zero in the first minute of sunlight

scenario.explanation: In light, photosynthesis uses CO₂ faster than respiration releases it, so CO₂ in the box decreases.

scenario.text: After a 100 m sprint, your legs burn and you breathe hard. Which explanation is BEST?

choices.label: Muscles made lactic acid when oxygen ran short
Muscles made extra glucose from carbon dioxide
Your lungs stopped working during the sprint race
Your cells did photosynthesis to make more energy

scenario.explanation: Muscles used anaerobic respiration, which makes lactic acid. Heavy breathing supplies oxygen to clear it and refill ATP.

scenario.text: Chewing rice for a long time makes it taste slightly sweet. Why?

choices.label: Saliva's amylase breaks starch into sugars
Teeth turn the rice into pure sugar crystals
Rice absorbs sugar from the air in the mouth
Chewing adds heat that melts the rice grains

scenario.explanation: Amylase is an enzyme that starts the catabolism of starch into simpler sugars right in the mouth.

choices.label: Building muscle proteins from amino acids
Digesting rice starch into simple glucose
Breaking down glucose to release ATP
Breaking down fat during a long fasting

scenario.explanation: Anabolism builds larger molecules and uses energy. The other three break molecules down (catabolism).

scenario.text: Bread dough with yeast rises when left in a warm place. What is happening?

choices.label: Yeast ferments sugar and releases CO₂
Heat makes the flour swell with steam
Yeast does photosynthesis inside the dough
Air from the room is soaked into the dough

scenario.explanation: Yeast breaks down sugar without oxygen (fermentation), releasing CO₂ bubbles that make the dough rise.

days.title: Why These Reactions Matter
days.content:
🌍 The Carbon–Oxygen Cycle

Photosynthesis removes CO₂ from the air and stores carbon in plants. Respiration, decay and burning return it. When we burn more fuel and cut more forests than plants can balance, CO₂ builds up in the atmosphere — a link to climate change you will study in Week 9.

🍚 Food, Energy and Health

  • The rice, bread and fruit we eat carry energy first captured by photosynthesis.
  • Cells release it through respiration; extra glucose is stored as glycogen or fat (anabolism).
  • Exercise increases respiration and oxygen demand; that is why heart rate and breathing rise.
  • When respiration cannot get enough oxygen (in a crowded, poorly ventilated room or at high altitude), people feel tired and dizzy.

🧠 Reading Equations as Stories

An equation tells you what goes in, what comes out, and in what amounts. For example, respiration says one glucose needs six O₂ and gives six CO₂ — so a person exercising hard both breathes in more oxygen and breathes out more carbon dioxide.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What does the arrow (→) in a chemical equation mean?

choices.label: React to form
Is equal in mass to
Is heated with
Is dissolved in

escape.explanation: The arrow separates reactants from products and is read as "react to form" or "yields."

escape.text: Which are the PRODUCTS of photosynthesis?

choices.label: Glucose and oxygen
Carbon dioxide and water
Glucose and carbon dioxide
Oxygen and energy (ATP)

escape.explanation: Photosynthesis turns CO₂ and water into glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and oxygen (O₂).

escape.text: Where does most cellular respiration take place?

choices.label: Mitochondria
Chloroplasts
Ribosomes
Cell wall

escape.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and produce most of the cell's ATP.

escape.text: How many oxygen atoms are on the right side of 6CO₂ + 6H₂O?
escape.explanation: 6CO₂ has 12 O atoms and 6H₂O has 6 O atoms: 12 + 6 = 18.

escape.text: Why do plants also carry out cellular respiration?

choices.label: Their cells need ATP day and night
They need to make extra glucose at night
Respiration replaces photosynthesis in sunlight
It lets plants absorb water from the soil air

escape.explanation: Every living cell needs ATP. Plants make glucose by photosynthesis and release its energy by respiration, at all times.

escape.text: When you exercise hard, why do you breathe out more CO₂?

choices.label: Faster respiration produces more CO₂
Your lungs make CO₂ from the air
Muscles store CO₂ and release it later
Sweat turns into carbon dioxide gas

escape.explanation: Respiration's products include CO₂. More respiration for more ATP means more CO₂ to exhale.
